$comment: mpad3 wire protocol — the single source of truth shared by firmware and host.
This file describes the SAME bytes that firmware/include/config.h and
firmware/include/magic.h describe in C. It is not generated from them and
they are not generated from it, because a generator that reads C structs
needs a C parser and a generator that emits C needs a template engine —
both are more machinery than this project should carry.
Instead the two are kept honest by a test on each side:
which is the real sizeof()/offsetof() output of the compiled C structs.
- `node host/tests/run.mjs` compares that file against THIS file and fails
on any mismatch, and independently re-implements CRC-16 and CRC-32 in
JavaScript and checks them against the same standard test vectors the C
So: if you change a struct in config.h, this file must change too, and the
test tells you so. All integers on the wire are little-endian.

fields.name: sof0
fields.note: 0xA5

fields.name: sof1
fields.note: 0x5A

fields.name: len
fields.note: payload byte count, little endian, 0..512

fields.name: crc16
fields.note: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over cmd..payload, little endian

crc.covers: bytes [2 .. 6+len) i.e. cmd, len, version, payload

0x00.name: PING
0x00.note: handshake; also proves the cable and the CDC interface are alive

0x02.name: GET_CONFIG
0x02.note: one request per chunk; chunkIndex must be 0..chunkCount-1

0x03.name: SET_CONFIG
0x03.response: SET_ACK on the final chunk only
0x03.note: streamed in order from chunk 0; applied to RAM on completion, written to flash only on COMMIT

0x04.name: RESET_CONFIG
0x04.note: factory defaults, written to flash immediately

0x05.name: COMMIT
0x05.note: write the staged RAM config to flash. Blocks ~50 ms during the erase.

0x07.name: SET_CHANNEL
0x07.note: out-of-range is refused with ERROR/BAD_ARG, not wrapped

0x09.name: SET_LIGHTING
0x09.note: marks config dirty for COMMIT even when physical LED drive is disabled; saved settings alone do not imply illuminated or current-approved hardware

0x0A.name: PREVIEW_LIGHTING
0x0A.note: volatile preview only when CAP_LED_OUTPUT is advertised; otherwise ERROR/LED_DISABLED without changing lighting. CAP_LED_OUTPUT is a bench compile flag, not a current or safety certification

0x0B.name: LED_TEST
0x0B.note: bench-only 9 x 3 exact RGB bytes, accepted only when CAP_LED_OUTPUT; otherwise ERROR/LED_DISABLED. Even when enabled it bypasses brightness and gamma and auto-expires after 300 ms; use a current-limited bench supply, not an unchecked USB rail

0x0C.name: OLED_FRAME
0x0C.note: Exactly two 265-byte payloads (index 0 then 1). The first half never replies; the final half alone yields a three-byte OLED_FRAME_ACK or one application ERROR. Parser-corrupt OLED packets have no reply and time out. A full-frame CRC-32 and per-packet framing CRC-16 prevent partial or mixed pixels. Baked screens reject frames.

0x8C.name: OLED_FRAME_ACK
0x8C.note: Only after BOTH halves and the full-frame CRC pass; acknowledges seq and mode.

0x0D.name: GET_OLED_STATE
0x0D.note: Read current physical screen and mode epoch after handshake; do not assume saved boot mode is the active mode.

0x0E.name: SET_OLED_MODE
0x0E.note: Select a physical screen (0..11); starts full dwell; rejected when no SSD1306 ACK; reply includes mode and epoch. Not a flash write.

0xC1.name: OLED_MODE_EVENT
0xC1.note: Unsolicited on actual physical mode change (manual, OLED_NEXT, auto timer, or host selection); coalesced under congestion, independent of KEY_EVENT setting.

0xFE.name: BOOTLOADER
0xFE.response: SET_ACK then the device reboots into BOOTSEL

fields.name: leds
fields.note: 9 on the full model; 0 on the keys-and-knob model. Config keeps nine lighting slots for wire compatibility; LED_OUTPUT reports whether physical data output is enabled.

fields.name: capabilities
fields.note: CAP_EVENTS means KEY_EVENT support even if global.usbReportEvents=0; read GET_CONFIG for the current stream setting.

fields.name: n
fields.note: byte count in this chunk; the last chunk is short

fields.name: rgb
fields.note: 9 LEDs x 3 bytes, in R,G,B order (NOT the strip's GRB — the firmware converts)

fields.name: value
fields.note: rotation detents; key HOLD_RELEASE: held duration in ms (0 on older firmware, capped at 32767)

fields.name: action
fields.note: actionType that fired, 0 if the slot was empty

fields.name: seq
fields.note: serial number modulo 65536; newer than last completed frame

fields.name: mode
fields.note: actual active runtime catalogue index; never baked

fields.name: index
fields.note: chunk 0 followed by chunk 1 (no interleaving)

fields.name: count
fields.note: always 2

fields.name: crc32
fields.note: IEEE CRC-32 of ALL 512 SSD1306 page-order bytes

fields.name: pages
fields.note: 256 bytes: first or second half of 4 pages x 128 columns

fields.name: epoch
fields.note: increments on actual screen changes; compare modulo 65536; no request ID

fields.name: mode
fields.note: catalogue index 0..11; no flash commit

action.note: One binding slot. Fixed size so the whole config stays flat and memcpy-able; the 4 trailing pad bytes are spare room for a parameter without a format bump.

fields.name: flags
fields.note: ORed bitmask

fields.name: code
fields.note: KEYCODE: (modifiers << 8) | HID usage, so one slot sends Ctrl+C; MEDIA: consumer usage; CHANNEL: channel index; LED_MODE: ledMode; LED_BRIGHT: 0-255. Meaning depends on type.

fields.name: text
fields.note: NUL-terminated; only meaningful for TEXT and WEBHOOK. Validation rejects an unterminated one.

fields.name: perKeyMask
fields.note: bit n set -> perKey[n] is used for key n instead of the base colour

fields.name: perKey
fields.note: 9 x RGB

channel.note: One complete page: 9 key bindings, 4 knob bindings, and that page's lighting.

fields.name: keys
fields.note: key index = position on the pad, left-to-right then top-to-bottom

fields.name: knobHold
fields.note: defaults to CHANNEL_NEXT, i.e. the page switch. It is a normal slot, so you CAN repoint it — and then you lose the only hardware way to change page.

fields.name: doubleTapMs
fields.note: 0 means double-tap is disabled, which makes a single tap fire on release with zero added latency. Do not set this to a non-zero value unless you actually bind a double tap: it delays every ordinary tap by that many milliseconds.

fields.name: knobIdleMs
fields.note: how long the knob must be still before a sub-batch rotation is delivered

fields.name: knobBatch
fields.note: detents accumulated before one rotation event is emitted

fields.name: ledInvertOutput
fields.note: legacy stored byte retained at default 1 for config compatibility; LED GPIO output-enable and data now always drive normally through the non-inverting 74AHCT1G125. This byte is ignored by the driver and must not be used to fix wiring

fields.name: oledAutoCycleS
fields.note: seconds each screen stays up before the panel rotates; 0 disables rotation. The panel has no touchscreen, so this timer is the default way it changes.

fields.name: oledPlaylist
fields.note: bit i = screen i in the rotation, in OLED_MODES order; 0 means every screen, which is what a config saved before this field existed reads as.

fields.name: oledBootMode
fields.note: catalogue mode index to show on power-up (0..11)

fields.name: oledContrast
fields.note: SSD1306 contrast register (0..255)

fields.name: oledInverted
fields.note: SSD1306 inverse pixels when 1

fields.name: oledPad
fields.note: reserved; must be zero

config.note: The v3 saved configuration streamed by SET_CONFIG. On boot firmware validates both CRCs of any older v2 A/B sectors, chooses the newest valid sequence and migrates into the other slot without erasing bindings; the host serial probe requires the matching v3 format before any write.

fields.name: crc32
fields.note: CRC-32/IEEE over bytes 0..2267 inclusive

sectorHeader.note: Prepended inside each of the two flash sectors, before the config blob.

fields.name: seq
fields.note: higher wins; this is what makes the A/B ping-pong work

fields.name: hdrCrc
fields.note: CRC-32 over the 12 bytes above

fields.name: seq
fields.note: serial number modulo 65536; newer than last completed frame

fields.name: mode
fields.note: actual active runtime catalogue index; never baked

fields.name: index
fields.note: chunk 0 followed by chunk 1 (no interleaving)

fields.name: count
fields.note: always 2

fields.name: crc32

status: A malformed frame is reported with the status that says *why*, not a single catch-all. `BAD_CRC` means the frame arrived intact in shape but the checksum did not match, which points at line noise or a byte dropped in transit. `BAD_LENGTH` means the declared payload length could not be satisfied, which points at a truncated write or a host encoder bug. `BAD_VERSION` means the frame was well formed and its `ver` byte is not one this firmware accepts, which points at an app built against a different protocol revision. The three have three different fixes, so an app should surface them differently rather than printing "bad frame".

Bytes that never formed a frame at all are dropped silently while the parser hunts for the `A5 5A` start-of-frame magic. The device does not reply to them: answering garbage would let one line glitch generate a flood of error frames.
capabilities: OLED_STREAM is advertised only while a physical SSD1306 ACKs on I2C. A compatible v3 app sends volatile runtime canvases at most 5 Hz, leaving baked loops autonomous. After 1200 ms without a complete frame the device renders its truthful offline screen. A partial frame expires after 350 ms; no frame writes flash.

LED_OUTPUT is advertised only for an explicitly bench-enabled firmware build. It means GPIO/PIO LED data is allowed; it does NOT attest to the actual cuttable strip, 5 V current budget, or electrical safety. Default firmware leaves GP10 LOW after initialization and rejects PREVIEW_LIGHTING/LED_TEST; this does NOT switch off LED 5 V, guarantee boot/reset levels, or clear a previously latched pixel. The strip and LED-only current budget remain unknown.

layout.ledIndexNote: LED n sits under key n, so the lighting array and the key array are indexed identically. That is a deliberate constraint: any per-key effect becomes a one-line lookup instead of a mapping table.

board.name: Waveshare RP2040-Zero
board.headerPins: 23 on the main castellated header: 5V, GND, 3V3, then 20 GPIO (GP0-GP15 and GP26-GP29)
board.notOnMainHeader: GP16 drives the board's own onboard WS2812. GP17-GP25 are on two 5-pin headers on the back and on solder pads, and are unused here
board.headerNumbering: USB-C up, front/component side facing you, pin 1 = 5V at top-left, counter-clockwise: left column 1-11 top to bottom (5V, GND, 3V3, GP29, GP28, GP27, GP26, GP15, GP14, GP13, GP12), right column 12-23 bottom to top (GP11, GP10, GP9, GP8, GP7, GP6, GP5, GP4, GP3, GP2, GP1, GP0)
board.spareHeaderGpio: GP13, GP14, GP15, GP26, GP27. GP28/GP29 carry required OLED I2C; only GP26/GP27 remain free as ADC inputs
board.configSectors: 0x1FE000 and 0x1FF000 - the last two 4 KiB sectors of the 2 MB flash

oledTransport: Version 2 added volatile OLED frame streaming; version 3 adds the fail-closed LED output capability and LED_DISABLED status. The saved config format remains version 3 (2,272 bytes). The host must verify PING/INFO plus CAP_OLED and CAP_OLED_STREAM before streaming. CAP_OLED_STREAM is advertised only while the SSD1306 ACKs at 0x3C. Older protocol-v1/v2 firmware is not compatible with this v3 app; update app and firmware together.

After handshake the app requests GET_OLED_STATE: [mode:u8, epoch:u16 LE]. OLED_MODE_EVENT (0xC1) carries the same payload whenever the physical playlist changes by timer, gesture, legacy text or host selection. Unlike OLED_STATE (0x8D), the unsolicited event cannot steal a pending reply. Epochs compare modulo 65536; stale events are ignored. The host does **not** send a mode command back in response to a device event, so the autonomous dwell is not restarted. SET_OLED_MODE selects a screen immediately and replies with OLED_STATE; only an explicit config Save persists its boot selection.

A runtime 128x32 frame is **512 bytes** in SSD1306 page order: byte page*128+x, bit y&7. The host sends two OLED_FRAME packets (265-byte payload each): seq:u16 LE, mode:u8, index:u8 (0 then 1), count:u8 (always 2), full-frame CRC-32/IEEE:u32 LE, pages[256]. Both have the ordinary MPAD3 CRC-16. Firmware bounds the first-half stage to 350 ms, checks current runtime mode and the full-frame CRC, then atomically publishes all 512 bytes and ACKs [seq:u16 LE, mode:u8]. No flash writes. If a packet is corrupt or an ACK is absent, the host skips/backoffs; it never reports a completed physical frame without the final ACK.

The host renders at **most 5 complete frames/second**, on a timer independent of the canvas preview or drawer visibility. Browsers can throttle a suspended tab; in that case the pad falls back offline. Frames are low priority: they do not queue behind a config/lighting request, and a user Save/mode selection waits for a short current stream slot. The pad locally plays all seven baked animations even with a PC attached. A layer-change overlay temporarily wins over live pixels. If complete frames stop, the last expires after **1,200 ms**, then the next 200-ms runtime refresh draws the truthful local fallback (uptime rather than fabricated wall time, -- for unknown metrics, NO MEDIA). On disconnect the host producer stops and no pixel data survives reboot.

Clock uses the connected PC wall clock; telemetry and media use the desktop OS integrations when available. Missing native data renders --/NO MEDIA, not invented readings. Custom labels stay stored on the PC, but are included in volatile Deck Status pixels while the app is connected. Source/fake-CDC tests are not proof of assembled-pad performance or a bootable UF2.
